walkthrough: We want to form 3-digit numbers using the digits $\{4, 5, 6, 7\}$ without repetition. For a number to be odd, its last digit must be an odd number. In this set, the odd digits are 5 and 7.
Split the counting into two mutually exclusive cases based on the last digit:

Case 1: The number ends in 5 ($**5$).
With 5 in the units position, there are 3 remaining digits available: $\{4, 6, 7\}$. We need to fill the hundreds and tens positions:
$$\text{Choices for hundreds: } 3, \quad \text{Choices for tens: } 2$$
$$\text{Ways} = 3 \times 2 = 6$$

Case 2: The number ends in 7 ($**7$).
With 7 in the units position, there are 3 remaining digits available: $\{4, 5, 6\}$. Filling hundreds and tens:
$$\text{Choices for hundreds: } 3, \quad \text{Choices for tens: } 2$$
$$\text{Ways} = 3 \times 2 = 6$$

Add the totals from both cases:
$$\text{Total 3-digit odd numbers} = 6 + 6 = 12$$
